extracted.intended_audience: lawyers, pro se litigants, and court staff who prepare or respond to appeals and petitions in the D.C. Court of Appeals
extracted.subtask_short: filing appeals in DC Court of Appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and requirements governing the composition, transmission, correction, and appendices of the record on appeal; transcripts; computing and extending time; in forma pauperis waivers; and petitions for review of agency decisions in the D.C. Court of Appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Record on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The following items constitute the record on appeal: (1) the original papers and exhibits filed in the Superior Court; (2) the transcript of proceedings, if any; and (3) a certified copy of the docket entries prepared by the Clerk of the Superior Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s Duty to Order Transcript
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days after filing the notice of appeal, the appellant must: (A) order from the reporter a transcript of such parts of the proceedings not already on file as the appellant considers necessary, and identify for the Court Reporter Division any transcript already prepared that is to be included in the record on appeal; or (B) file a certificate in this court stating that no transcript will be ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless proceeding under Rule 10(b)(5) (special in forma pauperis/criminal provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupported Finding or Conclusion — Transcript Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant intends to urge on appeal that a finding or conclusion is unsupported by the evidence or is contrary to the evidence, the appellant must include in the record a transcript of all evidence relevant to that finding or conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Cobb v. Standard Drug Co., 453 A.2d 110 (D.C. 1982).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial Transcript — Issue Statement and Designation Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the entire transcript is ordered: (A) the appellant must, within the 10 days provided in Rule 10(b)(1), file a statement of the issues to be presented on the appeal and serve on other parties a copy of the transcript order or certificate and the statement; (B) other parties may, within 10 days after service, file and serve a designation of additional parts to be ordered; and (C) unless within 10 days after service the appellant orders all such parts and notifies the parties, the designating party may within the following 10 days either order the parts or move in the Superior Court for an order requiring the appellant to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines are strict; parties may compel ordering through Superior Court if appellant fails to order designated parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment for Transcript
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of ordering, a party must make satisfactory arrangements with the Court Reporter Division for paying the cost of the transcript, except when the party is proceeding under Rule 10(b)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript Procedure for In Forma Pauperis / Criminal Justice Act / Prevention of Child Abuse Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Special provisions: (A) In civil cases where appellant has been granted a waiver of fees, a request for preparation of transcripts must be made, on motion with notice, to the appropriate motions or trial judge; (B) where appellant was permitted under the Criminal Justice Act, the notice of appeal will be treated as encompassing an order for preparation of the reporter’s transcript at government expense and a copy of the notice and docket entries will be transmitted to the Court Reporter Division for preparation; (C) counsel appointed under the Prevention of Child Abuse and Neglect Act must secure vouchers from the Finance Office and submit them to the trial judge for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 24(h) and applicable D.C. Code sections; the Criminal Justice Act transcript includes specified proceedings (pretrial hearings, voir dire, openings, testimony and evidence, closings, charge, verdict, sentencing, and other designated proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the Evidence When Proceedings Not Recorded
rubrics_metrics.description: If the transcript of a hearing or trial is unavailable, the appellant may prepare a statement of the evidence or proceedings from the best available means, including the appellant’s recollection. The statement must be served on all other parties, who may serve objections or proposed amendments within ten days. The statement and any objections or proposed amendments must be submitted to the trial judge for settlement and approval, and as settled and approved the statement must be included in the record on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed Statement as the Record on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: In place of the record on appeal as defined in Rule 10(a), the parties may prepare, sign, and submit to the trial judge a statement of the case showing how the issues arose and were decided in the Superior Court. The statement must set forth only those facts essential to the court’s resolution of the issues. If accurate, and with any additions the trial judge considers necessary, it must be approved, certified to the Court of Appeals, and may be filed in place of the appendix required by Rule 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or Modification of the Record
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Any difference about whether the record truly discloses what occurred must be submitted to and settled by the Superior Court and the record conformed accordingly. (2) If anything material is omitted or misstated in the record by error or accident, it may be corrected and a supplemental record certified and forwarded either (A) on a stipulation of the parties, or (B) by the Superior Court before or after the record has been forwarded. (3) All other questions as to the form and content of the record must be presented to this court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s Duty to Enable Assembly and Forwarding of Record
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant filing a notice of appeal must comply with Rule 10(b) and must do whatever else is necessary to enable the Clerk of the Superior Court to assemble and forward the record. If there are multiple appeals from a judgment or order, the Clerk must assemble a single record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter’s Duty to Prepare and File Transcript
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving an order for a transcript, the reporter must enter at the bottom of the order the date of its receipt and the expected completion date and send a copy, so endorsed, to the Clerk of the Superior Court; if the transcript cannot be completed within 60 days the reporter may request additional time from the court; when complete the reporter must file it with the Director of the Court Reporter Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director of the Court Reporter Division Duties
rubrics_metrics.description: If all transcript ordered or designated for appeal has not been completed within the 60-day period, the Director must retain the partial transcript until transcription of all proceedings is completed; when completed, transcripts must be placed in chronological sequence, properly renumbered, and filed with the Clerk of the Superior Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk of the Superior Court Duties on Record Transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) When the record is complete, the Clerk must prepare an index that reasonably identifies and numbers the documents constituting the record, and promptly send 4 certified copies of that index and the original reporter’s transcript, if any, to the Clerk of this court; the Clerk must retain all other parts of the record for the parties to use, subject to call by this court. In cases where a party was permitted to proceed in forma pauperis, the Clerk must prepare and submit 2 copies of the record. (B) If reporter’s transcript is filed after transmittal of the certified index, the Clerk must forward it as a supplemental record promptly after the Director files it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record for Preliminary Motions in the Court of Appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: If, before the record is forwarded, a party files in this court a motion for dismissal, summary reversal/affirmance, release pending appeal, stay/injunction pending appeal, additional security on a supersedeas bond, or other relief, the Clerk of the Superior Court, upon order of this court, must transmit a preliminary record containing the notices of appeal, the order appealed from, and those parts of the record designated by any party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards Governing Eligibility for Waiver (In Forma Pauperis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards governing eligibility for waiver are listed in D.C. Code § 15-712(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeding on Appeal In Forma Pauperis After Superior Court Permission
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who was permitted to proceed in forma pauperis or who was determined by the Superior Court to be eligible for court-appointed counsel may proceed on appeal in forma pauperis without further authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions/Applications for Waiver to be Filed in the Superior Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as stated in Rule 24(b)(1), a party seeking to take an appeal without prepayment must file in the Superior Court within the time for filing an appeal: (i) a notice of appeal containing the information prescribed in Form 1 or Form 2; and (ii) an application to waive court fees, costs, or security pursuant to Superior Court Rule of Civil Procedure 54-II — a motion and affidavit containing the information prescribed in Form 7a and Form 7b showing inability to pay fees or give security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Superior Court grants the waiver, the party may proceed without prepaying; if denied, the Superior Court must issue a written order stating reasons and the party may request a hearing under SCivR 54-II(j)(2) and thereafter may apply to this court.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFP Motion/Application to be Filed in the Court of Appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party desires to proceed on appeal in forma pauperis after having filed a notice of appeal and paid required fees, the party must file with this court an application to waive court costs, fees, or security (Form 7a) and sign the declaration contained in an affidavit (Form 7b).

rubrics_metrics.name: IFP Procedures for Petitions for Review of Agency Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When review of an agency order proceeds directly to this court, a party may file with the petition for review an application to waive court costs, fees, or security (Form 7) and sign the declaration; the waiver application and petition must be filed within the time permitted for seeking review of the agency order or decision. A party may file a motion to proceed in forma pauperis with the petition and an affidavit containing information prescribed in Form 7b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing is governed by the time permitted for review of the agency order; see Rule 15 for petition timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFP for Petitions for Extraordinary Writs
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who files a petition for an extraordinary writ and desires to proceed in forma pauperis must file, along with the petition, an application to waive court costs, fees, or security (Form 7a) and sign the declaration contained in an affidavit (Form 7b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Deciding Waiver Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Within 5 calendar days after receiving a completed waiver application, the court must decide whether to approve the application; the Clerk, if authorized, may grant waiver applications. (2) If, within 5 calendar days after receiving a completed application, the court has not ruled, the application will be deemed approved. (3) These deadlines do not apply where the court requires additional information under D.C. Code § 15-712(b)(1)(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of Waiver Application — Procedure and Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a waiver application is denied by this court, the court shall state the reasons for the denial or partial denial in writing. A party denied a waiver in whole or in part may request a hearing in accordance with D.C. Code § 15-712(c)(3)(A); a hearing must be held no later than 14 days after the court receives the hearing request. If, after the hearing, the waiver is denied, the party must pay the required filing fee within the time specified in the final order of denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits of Appeal Must Not Be Considered in Waiver Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering a waiver application, the court must not consider the merits of the appeal or petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for Free Transcripts or Other Documents (IFP)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Civil Cases: A party granted a waiver may file a motion in the Superior Court requesting that free transcripts or other documents be prepared and explaining the basis; the Superior Court must grant the motion unless the request is frivolous and may order only those portions necessary to resolution of the appeal. (2) Criminal Cases: For appellants permitted under the Criminal Justice Act, the notice of appeal will be treated as encompassing an order for preparation of the reporter’s transcript at government expense. In other criminal cases a defendant granted a waiver may file a motion in Superior Court requesting free transcripts, which will be addressed under Rule 10(b)(5)(B) procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superior Court must resolve doubt about frivolousness in favor of applicant (D.C. Code § 15-712(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of IFP Application and Financial Information
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The court must keep confidential an application and any financial information submitted pursuant to this rule or Superior Court Rule of Civil Procedure 54-II, except to the court, the litigant, persons authorized by the litigant, or by court order; the application must not be served on the other party. (2) Any person seeking access must file a motion, give notice to the litigant, and support it with a declaration showing good cause; any person granted access shall not reveal information except as authorized by law or court order. (3) The court’s decision on an application for a waiver shall not be confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Rules Governing In Forma Pauperis Appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: For rules specially governing in forma pauperis appeals, see Rules 10(b)(5), 11(b)(3), and 30(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the Appendix to the Briefs (Appellant’s Responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must prepare and file an appendix containing: (A) the relevant docket entries in the proceeding below; (B) the relevant pleadings, charge, findings, or opinion; (C) the judgment, order, or decision in question; and (D) other parts of the record to which the parties wish to direct the court’s attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded Material from the Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoranda of law filed in the Superior Court should not be included in the appendix unless they have independent relevance. Parts of the record may be relied on by the court or the parties even though not included in the appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to File Appendix and Number of Copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must file 4 copies of the appendix with the brief and must serve one copy on counsel for each party separately represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Parties’ Responsibilities in Determining Appendix Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Parties are encouraged to agree on contents. If no agreement, the appellant must, within 20 days after the Clerk notifies that the record is filed, serve on all other parties a designation of the parts the appellant intends to include and a statement of issues; any other party may, within 10 days after receiving the designation, serve a designation of additional parts, which the appellant must include. Parties must not engage in unnecessary designation of parts. This applies to cross-appellants and cross-appellees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of the Appendix; Allocation and Sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless parties agree otherwise, the appellant must pay the cost of the appendix. If the appellant considers parts designated by another party unnecessary, that party must advance the cost of including those parts. The cost of the appendix is a taxable cost. If any party causes unnecessary parts to be included, the court may impose the costs of those parts on that party and appropriate sanctions after notice and opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of the Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: The appendix must begin with a table of contents identifying the page at which each part begins; pages must be numbered consecutively; relevant docket entries must follow the table of contents and other parts must follow chronologically. When transcript pages are placed in the appendix, the date of each transcript and the page numbers must be listed on a separate page immediately before the included pages. Omissions in text must be indicated by asterisks. Immaterial formal matters (captions, subscriptions, acknowledgments, etc.) should be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction of Exhibits in Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits designated for inclusion may be reproduced in a separate volume(s), suitably indexed. Four copies must be filed with each copy of the appendix, and one copy must be served on counsel for each separately represented party. If a transcript of an administrative proceeding was used in the Superior Court and designated for inclusion, the transcript must be placed in the appendix as an exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal on the Original Record Without an Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: For good cause shown, the court may excuse a party from producing an appendix, or any part thereof, and permit an appeal to proceed on the original record with any copies of the record, or relevant parts, that the court may order the parties to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix in In Forma Pauperis Cases — Limited Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: No appendix is required in cases where a party has been permitted to proceed in forma pauperis or counsel has been appointed. In such cases: (1) The appellant must file with the brief 4 copies of any opinion, findings of fact, and conclusions of law, whether written or set forth orally in the transcript, that relate to the issues raised on appeal; and (2) The appellee may file with the brief 4 copies of any portions of the record to be called to the court’s attention that were not furnished by the appellant; (3) A copy of this document must be served on counsel for each party separately represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing Time — Basic Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Exclude the day of the act, event, or default that begins the period. (2) Exclude intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays when the period is less than 11 days, unless statute or court order provides otherwise, or unless the period is stated in calendar days. (3) Include the last day of the period unless it is a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday, or — if the act is filing a paper in court — a day on which the Clerk’s office is closed. (4) Definition of "legal holiday" includes a specified list (New Year’s Day, MLK Jr., Presidents’ Day, D.C. Emancipation Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans’ Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, and any other day appointed by the President/Congress or D.C.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extending Time
rubrics_metrics.description: For good cause, the court may extend the time prescribed by these rules to perform any act, or may permit an act to be done after that time expires. But the court may not extend the time: (1) to file a notice of appeal (except as authorized in Rule 4) or an application for allowance of appeal; (2) to file a petition for review; or (3) for doing any act when the time for doing the act has been prescribed by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Time After Certain Kinds of Service
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party is required or permitted to act within a prescribed period after a paper is served on that party, 5 calendar days are added to the prescribed period unless the paper is delivered on the date of service stated in the proof of service. For purposes of this rule, a paper that is served electronically is treated as delivered on the date of service stated in the proof of service. Rule 26(c) does not apply when an order of this court prescribes the time, and does not apply in determining timeliness of notices of appeal under Rules 4, 5, or 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Review — Filing and Form Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of an agency order or decision is commenced by filing with the Clerk an original and six copies of a petition for review. Unless an applicable statute provides otherwise, the petition must be filed within 30 days after notice is given in conformance with the agency's rules of the order or decision sought to be reviewed. If the time prescribed by statute is less than 11 days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays are excluded in the computation. If the order/decision is made out of the presence of parties and notice is by mail, the petitioner will have 5 additional days from date of mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Review — Content and Caption Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in Office of Administrative Hearings cases, the petition must: (A) name each party seeking review either in the caption or the body (terms like 'et al.' do not effectively name the parties); (B) name the agency as a respondent; and (C) specify the order or decision or part thereof to be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In OAH cases special rules apply: the petition must name each party seeking review and specify the order or decision to be reviewed; the petition may not name the OAH or the Administrative Law Judge as a respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by Mail and Signature Requirement for Petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing may be accomplished by mail addressed to the Clerk, but filing will not be deemed timely unless the petition is, in fact, received by the Clerk within the prescribed time. If the petitioner is a corporation or other entity, the petition must be signed by counsel; a petition not bearing the necessary signature will be stricken unless corrected promptly after being called to attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Petition for Review Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a timely petition for review is filed by a party, any other party to the agency proceeding may file a cross-petition for review within 14 days after the petition was filed, or within 30 days of the date of the challenged order or decision, whichever period expires later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 5 Suggested as Petition for Review Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 5 is a suggested form of a petition for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Duty to File Record; Time and Notice (Rule 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent agency must file the record within 60 days after being served with a petition for review. In cases involving review of an OAH decision, the OAH must file the record within 60 days of issuance of an order directing filing. The court may shorten or extend these deadlines for good cause. The Clerk must notify all parties and intervenors that the record has been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Constitutes Filing of the Record
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The agency must file: (A) the original or a certified copy of the record on review or parts designated by the parties; or (B) if a partial record is filed, a certified list adequately describing all documents, transcripts, exhibits, and other material constituting the record on review. (2) The parties may stipulate in writing that no record or certified list be filed; the date the stipulation is filed is treated as the date when the record is filed. (3) The agency must retain any portion of the record not filed with the Clerk; all parts retained are part of the record on review for all purposes and must be sent to the court if requested.
